name: Outcome
purpose: Tells the user that something has finished, such as signing in or out, with a short centred heading and line of text, and one action to go on.
when: Something the user did has finished, and they need to know before they go on, such as after signing out or signing in.
There is one obvious next step.
The screen ends a journey, or a step in one, and the user can't go back into it.

avoid.when: The user hasn't done it yet, and is choosing whether to.
The screen needs more than a line or two to explain things.
The user has more than one thing they could do next.
avoid.instead: Settings list, or a screen with a primary and a grouped secondary button in the button stack

screen: You’ve signed out, shown after signing out from Settings
notes: Say what happened in the heading, in the past tense, and what it means for the user in the text.
It has no navigation bar: the user goes on with its button, not back.
Its button goes nowhere of its own. The page listens for a click on it, by name, as examples/settings/signed-out.html does.
